brief.headline: Push for 60-day payment terms backed by their own 105-day vendor cycle, and qualify a direct-manufacturer second source to cut their reseller margin.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price cut to match a direct manufacturer's level, or open an RFQ to Manjushree and Mold-Tek for a maker price.
priceAsk.target: Target pricing in the ₹0.65–0.80/pc band for 28 mm caps at higher volume
priceAsk.basis: They are 100.0% a trader, so our price carries a reseller margin. The market ask for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap sits at ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec. Going direct to a maker strips that margin out.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 60 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Extending another 15 days frees up ₹2.68 L of cash for us; the full 30-day float we already use is worth ₹5.36 L.

brief.financialLeverage: They are weak — money-health score 2/10, in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.58), and keep only 2.8% as profit on every ₹100 they sell. But they already pay their own suppliers in 105 days versus 57 days for similar firms, and their own cash is stuck for just 1 day — so they can afford to wait longer for our payment. We're 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr in sales, a real chunk, so we have the weight to ask for better terms. Push hard on payment and on lining up a second source, but go easy on price — a big cut could tip them over and hurt our supply.

evidence.point: They are entirely a trader, not a maker
Market ask for 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume
They take 105 days to pay their own suppliers, far longer than the 57-day norm
Their overall money-health score is very low
They are in the grey distress zone

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — pharma bottles and caps direct from the maker, no reseller margin.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader at ₹946.50 Cr, health B (73/100) — strong, profitable, proven in pharma bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (lead to qualify)
alternates.why: A lead from public research, pan-India manufacturer — verify capability and pricing before issuing an RFQ.

risks: Their money-health score is 2/10 and they sit in the grey distress zone — supply continuity is at risk; don't load more volume onto them without a qualified backup.
They have pending legal case(s) on record — check what those are and whether they threaten operations or our contract.
They keep only 2.8% profit, so a heavy price squeeze could push them into the red and jeopardize supply — focus the win on payment terms and qualifying a second source.
100.0% of their revenue is traded goods — if their upstream supplier stumbles or hikes price, we feel it immediately; a direct-manufacturer alternate insulates us.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to 60-day payment terms — you're already taking 105 days with your own suppliers, so it's only fair — and we need you at a manufacturer's price or we'll RFQ this to Manjushree and Mold-Tek directly.
